Graph attrs via generics vdata / edata (defined R/00_graph_primitives.R). Isotopomer helpers: Molecule_igraph_add_isotopomer(), atom transfer via MCS RXNMapper.

title: AI_CONTEXT — MSCC
text: Isotope notation: [13]C, [2]H, [15]N, [18]O, [34]S (13C alone chemform APIs). Adduct strings: Prefer [M+H]+ / [M-H]-; many APIs also accept +/- polarity 0/1. Polarity: 0 = negative, 1 = positive (get_polarity_from_adduct, get_polarity_suffix). CFM collision energies: energy0→CE 10, energy1→CE 20, energy2→CE 40. RDKit: Import submodules explicitly (get_RDKit_Chem()); invent catch-get_RDKit(). CFM runtime: Prediction/annotation needs working CFM-ID Docker setup; local cache dirs supported. MSdev dependency: rely package MSdev (Imports/Suggests/Remotes, MSdev:: calls). MSdev already depends MSCC; adding reverse creates circular install loop. Use MSCC-local helpers migration_helpers.R CFM plotting via plotly_CFM_spectra() / shiny_vis_cfm(). Demo molecule: Glycine SMILES NCC(O)=O default several helpers.

title: AI_CONTEXT — MSCC
text: Vignettes: vignettes/MSCC.Rmd (stub), vignettes/CFM_shiny.qmd (CFM viewer usage). Informal tests/benchmarks: Test/TS.R (chemform_mz scaling). Man pages man/ roxygen-generated R/.

title: AI_CONTEXT — MSCC
text: Treat file read-unless user explicitly asks update . Prefer editing exported APIs roxygen docs together; regenerate NAMESPACE via roxygen, hand-edit. Keep formula/isotope parsing behavior stable; many downstream MS workflows depend string formats. dev_* files mix production exports experimental code — check @export / NAMESPACE assuming public API. Never add MSdev DESCRIPTION call MSdev:: MSCC — creates circular dependency (MSdev → MSCC already).

title: Rdisop mass decomposition
text: Quick reference Rdisop turns exact mass (isotope pattern) candidate sum formulas, fits formula-calculator workflow. Algorithms: Böcker et al. (DECOMP / Money Changing Problem). See Bioconductor vignette Mass decomposition Rdisop package.

title: Rdisop mass decomposition
text: Decide explicitly whether input ion m/z neutral mass. mix “neutral mass + z = 1” unless intentional. MSdev / MSCC split:
code: m/z + polarity/adduct + ppm + element set         ↓ 1. Convert ion m/z → neutral (or charged) mass consistently         ↓ 2. Enumerate formulas (Rdisop::decomposeMass / decomposeIsotopes)         ↓ 3. Filter chemically (parity, H/C, heteroatom rules, DBE / Senior)         ↓ 4. Rank (ppm, RDBe, isotope fit if MS1 pattern available)         ↓ 5. Return tidy table of candidates

title: Rdisop mass decomposition
text: decomposeMass thin wrapper: Core problem (Money Changing Problem / MCP): Find non-negative integers (nC,nH,nN,…)(n_C, n_H, n_N, \ldots) ∑ne⋅\sum n_e \cdot m_e lies within mass tolerance window. Typical R call: Useful accessors: getFormula(), getMass(), getScore(), getValid(), getIsotope(). measured isotope peaks, prefer decomposeIsotopes(masses, intensities, ...) — enumeration core, better ranking.
code: decomposeMass(mass, ppm, ...)   → decomposeIsotopes(c(mass), intensity = 1, ...)   → C++ Money-Changing / mass-decomposition solver library(Rdisop)  elements <- initializeElements(c("C", "H", "N", "O")) results <- decomposeMass(   mass = 203.0526,   ppm = 5,   z = 1,   elements = elements ) getFormula(results)

what: 3.2 Real masses → integers (what Rdisop / imslib actually do)
title: Rdisop mass decomposition
text: Monoisotopic masses real numbers (e.g. mC=12.000000m_\mathrm{C} = 12.000000, mH=1.007825m_\mathrm{H} = 1.007825). pipeline : Tolerance real mass: 𝚊𝚋𝚜_𝚎𝚛𝚛𝚘𝚛=𝚙𝚙𝚖⋅𝚖𝚊𝚜𝚜⋅10−6+𝚖𝚣𝚊𝚋𝚜 \texttt{abs\_error} = \texttt{ppm} \cdot \texttt{mass} \cdot 10^{-6} + \texttt{mzabs} RealMassDecomposer widens integer search range slightly using precomputed min/max weight rounding errors, re-checks candidate true real mass false positives scaling dropped.
code: element alphabet (mono masses m_i)         │         ▼ scale by precision (Rdisop default ~ 1e-5 Da)   w_i = round(m_i / precision)   → integer Weights         │         ▼ optional divide-by-GCD (shrink integers without changing solutions)         │         ▼ RealMassDecomposer   1. expand tolerance window for rounding error   2. for each integer mass M in [M_lo, M_hi):        IntegerMassDecomposer → all n with Σ n·w = M   3. keep only those with |Σ n·m_i − mass| ≤ abs_error         │         ▼ formula strings + exact masses (real Σ n·m_i)

title: Rdisop mass decomposition
text: Keep alphabet small (CHNO CHNOPS first). Tighten ppm / mzabs. Use minElements / maxElements cap atom counts. Prefer decomposeIsotopes M+1 / M+2 intensities exist. Post-filter (H/C ranges, RDBE, nitrogen rule) keep top-NN ppm / score. Expect sharp jump candidates adding Cl, Br, metals, many heteroatoms.

title: Seven Golden Rules
text: Hard upper bounds C, H, N, O, P, S, … mass window, derived DNP / Wiley-type formula sets (bare mass / element_mass). calcMF (maxCounts): uses DNP-style caps (higher DNP vs Wiley paper’s Table 1 CHNOPS; halogens DNP): Also: Filters$minElements / maxElements (passed decomposeMass).

previous_headings: Seven Golden Rules (Kind & Fiehn) and MassTools::calcMF > The seven rules (summary)
title: Seven Golden Rules
text: LEWIS (octet / valence): atoms filled valence shells; strict enforcement rejects odd-electron species (e.g. many nitroso / radicals). Often relaxed via DBE / parity. SENIOR (molecular graph): formula exist connected graph, Sum valences (count odd-valence atoms) even Sum valences ≥ 2 × maximum valence Sum valences ≥ 2 × (number atoms − 1) calcMF (SeniorRule): implements Senior’s third condition : Default keep SENIOR3 >= 0 (Filters$SENIOR3 = 0). Uses maximum valence states per element (Kind & Fiehn). Extra related filters (numbered golden rules): Filters$DBErange (default −5…40), Filters$parity ("e" / "o").
code: SENIOR3 = Σ (count × max_valence) − 2 × (n_atoms − 1)
